newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Tudela lauds raid, blames "stubborn" MRTA.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Tudela lauds raid, blames "stubborn" MRTA.

text.p: Peruvian Foreign Minister Francisco Tudela, a freed hostage, on Friday said the guerrillas' impossible demands forced a military strike on the Japanese ambassador's home and called the raid "impeccable."

"I want to express my public recognition to the president of the Republic (Alberto Fujimori) and to our armed forces for the impeccable operation which allowed our liberation," Tudela said in a statement from a hospital bed.
"I find it unfortunate that the stubborness of the terrorists in demanding impossible goals made it necessary to resort, as a last option, to force," Tudela said.

His strong support for the strike followed mounting reports that some of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels who held hostages in the residence were executed after being captured or while trying to surrender.
Tudela has been recovering from gunshot wounds he received in Tuesday's raid on the Japanese ambassador's residence, in which he and 70 other hostages were rescued by army commandos.

Japanese Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda visited Tudela in Lima's military hospital, together with Teresuke Terada, Japan's official observer in the ultimately fruitless talks to end the siege peacefully.
In Tuesday's raid, only one hostage died, along with two commandos and all 14 MRTA rebels.

Tudela said he would resume his duties as foreign minister as soon as his health allowed. He praised the "heroic and brave action" of army commando Juan Valer, who was killed by MRTA gunfire as he tried to shield Tudela -- the MRTA's prize hostage -- while he ran out of the burning residence.
One of the most searing images of the raid was Tudela staggering out a side door of mansion, holding his bloodied shoulder as bombs exploded around the house.
